digest.component_or_area: Cloud Jira adapter resilience and config-validation coverage
propositions: Cloud transport has no enumerated per-member 429 retry sweep, leaving mutations at undocumented retry layers undetected (DC's tier-2 coverage does not transfer uniformly across four distinct 429 behaviors split across two dispatch levels)
Cloud lacks config-validation tests for non-HTTPS rejection, missing-credential loudness, and resolved-status configurability, gaps that DC's hardening addressed but Cloud never adopted
Cloud's hardcoded RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES has no runtime config hook and no clear decision on whether Cloud deployments using non-standard workflow states need one for parity with DC
Cloud's user-search-method degradation path is untested on DC; the absence of any three user-search aliases in DC should be pinned to prevent accidental regressions on the Cloud side

Each mutating Cloud transport member must be classified by seam (ACLI subprocess vs pooled REST vs bare urlopen) and dispatch level (retrying wrapper vs non-retrying phases vs no wrapper) to establish correct 429 assertions and duplicate-write safety

Bare-urlopen members like acli_cli_ops.update_priority bypass _rest_urlopen_with_retry's transient-fault retry entirely, creating a third HTTP mutation path with distinct behavior not covered by existing 429 tests
